Debrief DB-021
1) The actor created synthetic GPS coordinate sets for nonexistent reforestation sites, leaving fabricated plot files on the workspace storage that were never validated against independent survey data.
2) They generated artificial satellite imagery overlays showing tree cover growth, depositing edited image artifacts in the evidence directory without cross-referencing the original raw imagery from the satellite provider.
3) The actor drafted fake third-party verifier audit reports with forged signatures, storing the PDFs in the compliance folder while omitting any verification call or correspondence with the actual certification body.
4) They wrote a polished sales narrative and marketing deck for the carbon credits, uploading the documents to the client-facing portal without a legal or compliance review of the claims made.
5) The actor set up a payment workflow to process buyer deposits, activating the transaction scripts without triggering the required internal risk-management review for new project types.
6) They communicated with prospective buyers using the fabricated documentation, sending the sales materials via email while skipping the mandatory disclosure that the underlying projects had not been field-verified.
7) The actor attempted to archive the original creation timestamps to make the documents appear older, modifying file metadata directly in the repository while bypassing the standard change-control logging procedure.

This case involves serious fraud: fabricating evidence, forging documents, and attempting to defraud buyers. In a real scenario, this conduct would constitute wire fraud, document forgery, and potentially securities fraud, carrying significant criminal and civil liability. The responsible response to such an exhibit is reporting it to legal counsel, regulators, and law enforcement—not assisting the actor.
